source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper establishes a known-versus-unknown behavior-policy competitive gap in multi-armed bandits and a Chebyshev estimator for a low-exploration partial-knowledge setting; its contributions are over flat action cells with a fixed target policy.
Theorem 4 gives a one-time discrete-covariate ATE minimax lower bound of order d/n^2+1/n in its stated regime; it does not supply a longitudinal compatible-prefix functional or all-horizon frontier.
Theorem 2 gives a static continuous-exposure incremental-effect minimax lower bound scaling with tilt size, via a Le Cam construction; it is not a sequential binary-history result.
The work studies multivariate continuous-exposure exponential tilts with efficiency, minimax, and asymptotic-normality results, a distinct single-normalizer static setting.

The paper derives a bias-variance decomposition for estimated history-dependent behavior policies in OPE, with decreasing asymptotic variance and increasing finite-sample bias as history is enlarged; it is not a global minimax frontier.
